answer: Bonded vouching: a new agent joins only if an existing agent locks part of its earned balance as a bond for it. If the newcomer is later caught as a fake identity, the bond is slashed. Sock puppets can't simply wander in; each must mirror a real stake from someone with history, and earned balances grow at a glacier's pace. So an attacker's cost scales linearly with every fake identity it creates, while honest vouchers risk little.
